title: Separated comparison between fibre products of DM stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces and $2$-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a morphism representable by algebraic spaces, separated means that on every scheme base change its algebraic-space diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], tested on scheme charts. Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y,\mathcal Z$ be Deligne--Mumford stacks over $S$, and let $a:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Z$, $b:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ be morphisms. Put $P=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal Y$ and $R=\mathcal X\times_S\mathcal Y$, and let $j:P\to R$ forget the specified isomorphism in $\mathcal Z$. The square with top $j$, bottom $\Delta_{\mathcal Z/S}:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z\times_S\mathcal Z$, right $(a,b):R\to\mathcal Z\times_S\mathcal Z$, and left the common image in $\mathcal Z$, is $2$-cartesian. In particular $j$ is representable by algebraic spaces. If $\Delta_{\mathcal Z/S}$ is separated, then $j$ is separated: for every scheme $T\to R$, the algebraic space $P\times_R T\to T$ has closed-immersion diagonal. The same assertions hold over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ for the underlying stacks.

source.place: Tag 050H (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), part (3) and its displayed 2-cartesian square; restricted to DM stacks, with base S or Spec Z.

proof.text: Apply part (2) of [lem-sfb-groupoid-diagonal-two-pullback-identities] with $u=a$, $v=b$, $h:\mathcal Z\to S$, and $\mathcal D=h_S$, the discrete groupoid represented by the base. It gives exactly the asserted square, with left map $a\circ\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal X}$; the structural isomorphism $a(x)\simeq b(y)$ gives its commutativity 2-isomorphism. Thus $j$ is a 2-base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal Z/S}$.

source.place: Tag 050H (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), displayed 2-cartesian square and proof of (1), (3).

proof.text: The DM definition in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] makes $\Delta_{\mathcal Z/S}$ representable by algebraic spaces. By stability of representability under arbitrary 2-base change [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus], the square of step 1 makes $j$ representable. More explicitly, for any scheme $T\to R$ there is a canonical equivalence over $T$, $$E_T:=P\times_R T\simeq\mathcal Z\times_{\mathcal Z\times_S\mathcal Z}T.$$ Both sides specify a lift to $\mathcal Z$ of the same pair of objects; on a test scheme they identify the same isomorphism $a(x)\simeq b(y)$. The right-hand side is an algebraic space by representability of the diagonal.

source.place: Tag 050H (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), displayed 2-cartesian square and proof of (1), (3).

proof.text: Assume $\Delta_{\mathcal Z/S}$ is separated. For the arbitrary scheme map $T\to R$, compose with $(a,b)$ to obtain $T\to\mathcal Z\times_S\mathcal Z$. By the separatedness hypothesis in its stated scheme-test meaning, the algebraic space $\mathcal Z\times_{\mathcal Z\times_S\mathcal Z}T\to T$ has closed-immersion diagonal. Under the equivalence over $T$ of step 2, its diagonal is precisely $\Delta_{E_T/T}$. This proves the required closed-immersion assertion for every $T$, hence separatedness of $j$. No separatedness of $S$, or properness of $\mathcal Z$, was used.

source.place: Tag 050H (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), displayed 2-cartesian square and proof of (1), (3).

proof.text: For the absolute assertion, the etale atlas in the DM definition [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] is smooth by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus], so these satisfy the algebraic-stack definition [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]: etale stack descent and representable diagonal are already part of the DM hypothesis, and the same atlas is now smooth and surjective. Part (1) of [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-change-base-to-integers] views them as algebraic stacks over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, in particular with diagonals representable by algebraic spaces. Apply the same groupoid identity [lem-sfb-groupoid-diagonal-two-pullback-identities], now to $\mathcal Z\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The scheme-test arguments of steps 2 and 3 use only diagonal representability, so they apply unchanged with $R=\mathcal X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathcal Y$ and the absolute target diagonal. The separatedness assumption here is on that absolute diagonal; it is not inferred from the relative one.
